title: PostgreSQL
label: PostgreSQL
desc: Relational database with MVCC, a rich SQL dialect, JSONB, extensions and strong consistency guarantees.

sections.title: Setup
sections.description: Install the server, start it and confirm the cluster answers.

snippets.code:
# Debian or Ubuntu: server plus contrib modules
sudo apt update
sudo apt install postgresql postgresql-contrib
sudo systemctl enable --now postgresql

# Fedora and RHEL: the init step is explicit
sudo dnf install postgresql-server postgresql-contrib
sudo postgresql-setup --initdb
sudo systemctl enable --now postgresql

# Arch: the package makes the user, the cluster is initialised by hand
sudo pacman -S postgresql
sudo -u postgres initdb -D /var/lib/postgres/data
sudo systemctl enable --now postgresql

# Alpine
sudo apk add postgresql16 postgresql16-client

# The package creates a cluster and a postgres superuser
sudo -u postgres psql -c "SELECT version();"

# macOS with Homebrew
brew install postgresql@17
brew services start postgresql@17
export PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/postgresql@17/bin:$PATH"
psql postgres -c "SELECT version();"

# Container with a password and a named volume
docker run --name pg17 \
  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=devsecret \
  -e POSTGRES_DB=inventory \
  -p 5432:5432 \
  -v pg17-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data \
  -d postgres:17

# Wait until the port accepts connections
pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5432 -U app_user

sections.title: Connection
sections.description: Reach a database by URI, environment or password file and inspect the session.

snippets.code:
# URI form: user, password, host, port, database
psql "postgresql://app_user:devsecret@127.0.0.1:5432/inventory?sslmode=require"

# The same connection through environment variables
export PGHOST=127.0.0.1
export PGPORT=5432
export PGUSER=app_user
export PGDATABASE=inventory
psql -c "SELECT 1;"

# Keep the password out of the shell history and out of ps output
# format: host:port:database:user:password
printf '127.0.0.1:5432:inventory:app_user:devsecret\n' >> ~/.pgpass
chmod 600 ~/.pgpass
psql -h 127.0.0.1 -U app_user -d inventory

-- Who am I, where am I, and which server answered
SELECT current_database() AS database,
       current_user AS login,
       current_schema() AS schema,
       inet_server_addr() AS server_ip,
       inet_server_port() AS server_port,
       version() AS server_version;

sections.title: psql Basics
sections.description: Meta-commands, scripted runs and client-side file loading.

snippets.code:
\l                 list databases
\c inventory       connect to another database
\dn                list schemas
\dt public.*       list tables in one schema
\dv                list views
\df+ round         describe functions named round
\d+ orders         columns, indexes, constraints and storage
\du                list roles
\x auto            expand wide output automatically
\timing on         print execution time
\e                 edit the last query in $EDITOR
\i schema.sql      run a file on the client side
\copy customers (email, display_name) FROM 'customers.csv' WITH (FORMAT csv, HEADER true)
\q                 quit

# Run a script and stop at the first error
psql -h 127.0.0.1 -U app_user -d inventory \
  -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 \
  -f migrations/001_init.sql

# Unaligned, tuples only: useful inside shell pipelines
psql -h 127.0.0.1 -U app_user -d inventory \
  -Atc "SELECT count(*) FROM orders;"

sections.title: Databases and Schemas
sections.description: Create databases and schemas, then inspect their size and ownership.

sections.title: Tables
sections.description: Define tables with identity keys, constraints and partitions, then alter them safely.

sections.title: Data Types
sections.description: Pick exact numbers, time-zone-aware timestamps, arrays and custom enum types.

snippets.code:
-- Money as integer cents, ratings as exact decimal, time as timestamptz
CREATE TABLE type_demo (
  id          bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  quantity    integer NOT NULL,
  unit_cents  integer NOT NULL,
  rating      numeric(3, 2) CHECK (rating BETWEEN 0 AND 5),
  label       text NOT NULL,
  code        varchar(12) NOT NULL,
  active      boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  born_on     date,
  seen_at     timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  tags        text[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  payload     jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb
);

SELECT
  '42'::integer AS from_text,
  now()::date AS today,
  CAST('2026-11-04' AS date) AS explicit_cast,
  '2 days 03:30:00'::interval AS duration,
  7 / 2 AS integer_division,
  7::numeric / 2 AS numeric_division,
  round(2.675::numeric, 2) AS rounded;

-- timestamptz stores an instant; the session decides how to render it
SET TIME ZONE 'America/Sao_Paulo';
SELECT now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AS utc_clock;

sections.title: Inserting Rows
sections.description: Insert many rows, upsert on conflict and copy data in bulk.

snippets.code:
INSERT INTO customers (email, full_name)
VALUES ('ana@example.com', 'Ana Souza'),
       ('bruno@example.com', 'Bruno Lima'),
       ('carla@example.com', 'Carla Nunes')
RETURNING id, email;

-- One row per email: update the existing row instead of failing
INSERT INTO customers (email, full_name)
VALUES ('ana@example.com', 'Ana Souza')
ON CONFLICT (email) DO UPDATE
SET full_name = EXCLUDED.full_name
RETURNING id, email;

-- Keep explicit ids when copying from a legacy system
INSERT INTO customers (id, email, full_name)
OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE
VALUES (9001, 'dave@example.com', 'Dave Park');

-- Move old rows into an archive table
INSERT INTO customers_archive (id, email, full_name)
SELECT id, email, full_name
FROM customers
WHERE created_at < '2025-01-01';

-- Bulk load a file that lives on the server, not on the client
COPY customers (email, full_name)
FROM '/srv/import/customers.csv'
WITH (FORMAT csv, HEADER true);

sections.title: Selecting Rows
sections.description: Project columns, compute expressions and page through ordered results.

snippets.code:
SELECT id,
       email,
       created_at
FROM customers
ORDER BY created_at DESC
LIMIT 20 OFFSET 40;

SELECT id,
       status,
       coalesce(shipped_at, placed_at) AS last_event,
       total_cents / 100.0 AS total,
       date_trunc('day', placed_at) AS day
FROM orders
WHERE status = 'paid'
ORDER BY placed_at DESC;

SELECT 2 + 3 AS sum,
       '2026-11-04'::date + 7 AS next_week,
       concat('order-', 42) AS reference,
       nullif('', '') IS NULL AS empty_is_null,
       split_part('ana@example.com', '@', 2) AS domain;

sections.title: Filtering and Sorting
sections.description: Combine predicates, pattern matching and deterministic ordering.

snippets.code:
-- Half-open range catches every timestamp in 2026
SELECT id, email, created_at
FROM customers
WHERE created_at >= '2026-01-01'
  AND created_at <  '2027-01-01'
  AND email ILIKE '%@example.com'
  AND full_name IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY created_at;

SELECT id, status, total_cents
FROM orders
WHERE status IN ('pending', 'paid')
  AND total_cents BETWEEN 1000 AND 50000
  AND shipped_at IS NULL
ORDER BY total_cents DESC NULLS LAST, id ASC
LIMIT 25;

-- Latest order per customer, one row each
SELECT DISTINCT ON (customer_id)
       customer_id, id, placed_at
FROM orders
ORDER BY customer_id, placed_at DESC;

sections.title: Joins
sections.description: Combine tables with inner, outer and lateral joins.

snippets.code:
SELECT o.id,
       c.email,
       o.total_cents,
       o.placed_at
FROM orders AS o
JOIN customers AS c ON c.id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.status = 'paid'
ORDER BY o.placed_at DESC;

-- Every customer, including those with no orders
SELECT c.id, c.email, count(o.id) AS orders
FROM customers AS c
LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.id, c.email
ORDER BY orders DESC;

-- Anti-join: customers who never ordered
SELECT c.id, c.email
FROM customers AS c
LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id
WHERE o.id IS NULL;

-- Three most recent orders for each customer
SELECT c.email, recent.id AS order_id, recent.total_cents
FROM customers AS c
CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT o.id, o.total_cents
  FROM orders AS o
  WHERE o.customer_id = c.id
  ORDER BY o.placed_at DESC
  LIMIT 3
) AS recent
ORDER BY c.email, recent.id;

sections.title: Aggregation and Grouping
sections.description: Count, filter aggregates, group by expressions and build totals.

snippets.code:
SELECT count(*) AS all_rows,
       count(shipped_at) AS shipped_rows,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'paid') AS paid_rows,
       avg(total_cents) AS avg_cents
FROM orders;

SELECT date_trunc('month', placed_at) AS month,
       count(*) AS orders,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'paid') AS paid,
       sum(total_cents) / 100.0 AS revenue
FROM orders
WHERE placed_at >= '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY 1
HAVING count(*) >= 5
ORDER BY 1;

SELECT c.email,
       string_agg(o.id::text, ', ' ORDER BY o.placed_at) AS order_ids,
       array_agg(o.total_cents ORDER BY o.placed_at) AS totals
FROM customers AS c
JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.email;

-- Per status plus a grand total row
SELECT status, sum(total_cents) AS cents
FROM orders
GROUP BY ROLLUP (status)
ORDER BY status NULLS LAST;

sections.title: Window Functions
sections.description: Rank rows, compute running totals and compare neighbours without collapsing them.

snippets.code:
SELECT customer_id,
       id,
       placed_at,
       row_number() OVER (
         PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY placed_at DESC
       ) AS recency,
       sum(total_cents) OVER (
         PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY placed_at
         ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
       ) AS running_cents
FROM orders;

sections.title: Common Table Expressions
sections.description: Name intermediate results, walk hierarchies and modify data in one statement.

snippets.code:
WITH paid AS (
  SELECT customer_id, sum(total_cents) AS cents
  FROM orders
  WHERE status = 'paid'
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT c.email, paid.cents
FROM paid
JOIN customers AS c ON c.id = paid.customer_id
ORDER BY paid.cents DESC;

WITH RECURSIVE tree AS (
  SELECT id, parent_id, name, 1 AS depth
  FROM categories
  WHERE parent_id IS NULL

  UNION ALL

  SELECT c.id, c.parent_id, c.name, t.depth + 1
  FROM categories AS c
  JOIN tree AS t ON c.parent_id = t.id
)
SELECT depth, repeat('  ', depth - 1) || name AS path
FROM tree
ORDER BY path;

-- Move cancelled orders to an archive in one statement
WITH moved AS (
  DELETE FROM orders
  WHERE status = 'cancelled'
  RETURNING id, customer_id, status, total_cents, placed_at
)
INSERT INTO orders_archive (id, customer_id, status, total_cents, placed_at)
SELECT id, customer_id, status, total_cents, placed_at
FROM moved;

sections.title: EXPLAIN and Performance
sections.description: Measure a plan with real buffers, refresh statistics and find slow statements.

snippets.code:
-- ANALYZE executes the query; BUFFERS shows cache hits and disk reads
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)
SELECT o.id, o.total_cents
FROM orders AS o
WHERE o.customer_id = 42
ORDER BY o.placed_at DESC
LIMIT 10;

-- Refresh planner statistics after a large load
VACUUM (ANALYZE) orders;
ANALYZE customers;

-- Slowest statements by total time, once pg_stat_statements is loaded
SELECT calls,
       round(total_exec_time::numeric, 1) AS total_ms,
       round(mean_exec_time::numeric, 1) AS mean_ms,
       rows,
       query
FROM pg_stat_statements
ORDER BY total_exec_time DESC
LIMIT 10;

-- Compare estimated rows with actual rows for one node
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, VERBOSE, COSTS OFF)
SELECT count(*)
FROM orders
WHERE status = 'paid';

sections.title: Transactions
sections.description: Group statements atomically, roll back partially and claim rows without waiting.

snippets.code:
-- One worker claims a job without waiting for another worker
WITH job AS (
  SELECT id
  FROM jobs
  WHERE status = 'queued'
  ORDER BY created_at
  FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
  LIMIT 1
)
UPDATE jobs
SET status = 'running'
WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM job)
RETURNING id;

sections.title: Backup and Restore
sections.description: Dump logical backups in several formats and take a physical base backup.

snippets.code:
# Custom format: compressed single file, selective restore
pg_dump -h 127.0.0.1 -U app_user -d inventory -Fc -f inventory.dump

# Inspect what the dump contains before restoring
pg_restore --list inventory.dump | head -20

# Directory format allows parallel dump and restore
pg_dump -h 127.0.0.1 -U app_user -d inventory -Fd -j 4 -f inventory_dir

createdb -h 127.0.0.1 -U app_user inventory_restore
pg_restore -h 127.0.0.1 -U app_user \
  -d inventory_restore \
  -j 4 \
  inventory_dir

# Plain SQL compressed on the fly; the result is portable text
pg_dump -h 127.0.0.1 -U app_user -d inventory | gzip > inventory.sql.gz
gunzip -c inventory.sql.gz | psql -h 127.0.0.1 -U app_user -d inventory_restore

# Roles and tablespaces only
pg_dumpall -h 127.0.0.1 -U postgres --globals-only > globals.sql

# Physical backup of the whole cluster as compressed tar
pg_basebackup -h 127.0.0.1 -U replicator -D /srv/backup/base -Ft -z -P

sections.title: Extensions
sections.description: List available modules, add trigram search and load server instrumentation.

snippets.code:
-- What is installed and which version is loaded
SELECT extname, extversion
FROM pg_extension
ORDER BY extname;

-- What the server can install
SELECT name, default_version
FROM pg_available_extensions
WHERE name IN ('pg_trgm', 'pg_stat_statements', 'postgis', 'pgcrypto')
ORDER BY name;

sections.title: JSON and JSONB
sections.description: Extract, filter, expand and rebuild JSONB documents with operators and functions.

snippets.code:
SELECT id,
       payload->>'status' AS status,
       payload->'customer'->>'email' AS email,
       payload->'items'->0->>'sku' AS first_sku
FROM events
WHERE payload @> '{"status": "paid"}';

-- Expand an array into one row per element
SELECT e.id,
       item->>'sku' AS sku,
       (item->>'qty')::integer AS qty
FROM events AS e
CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(e.payload->'items') AS item;

-- Merge a patch into an object, then drop one key
UPDATE events
SET payload = (payload || '{"status": "shipped"}'::jsonb) - 'retries'
WHERE id = 42
RETURNING payload;

-- Build one document per customer from relational rows
SELECT jsonb_build_object(
         'customer', c.email,
         'orders', jsonb_agg(
           jsonb_build_object('id', o.id, 'cents', o.total_cents)
           ORDER BY o.placed_at
         )
       ) AS document
FROM customers AS c
JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id
WHERE c.id = 42
GROUP BY c.email;

sections.title: Common Errors
sections.description: Recognise frequent failures and the check that settles each one.

snippets.code:
FATAL: password authentication failed for user "app_user"
  check pg_hba.conf uses scram-sha-256 and that the role has a password

FATAL: no pg_hba.conf entry for host "10.0.0.5", user "app_user", database "inventory"
  add a host line for 10.0.0.0/24 and reload the configuration

ERROR: relation "orders" does not exist
  check current_schema() and search_path, or qualify the name as public.orders

ERROR: deadlock detected
  take locks in the same order everywhere and keep transactions short

ERROR: could not serialize access due to concurrent update
  retry the transaction; SERIALIZABLE and REPEATABLE READ can abort by design
